newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher across the board.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Wednesday, as local investors were encouraged by higher soybean prices and the yen's weaker tone against the dollar, traders said.
Prices were 140 to 210 yen higher, with the benchmark May 1998 contract up 140 at 15,790 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 42,742 lots.
Most contracts were weaker at the opening, but gradually rose by late morning on buying from local investors, traders said. Trade was basically quiet due to Japan's "Golden Week" holiday, they said.
The spot May contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.93-1/2 per bushel at 0810 GMT, up from $2.91-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
Spot May CBOT soybean futures were at $8.77-1/4 a bushel, up from $8.67-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
